title: Gradient-Guided Density Peak Clustering
summary: Density peak clustering links each point to its nearest higher-density neighbor, but these 1NN uphill paths can be unstable and produce irregular cluster boundaries. GGDPC inserts a one-step gradient-ascent update before each 1NN uphill search, while keeping the higher-density constraint anchored at the original observation, and builds clustering, decision-diagram, waterfall, and dendrogram summaries from the resulting graph. The paper proves consistency under five complementary criteria and reports competitive ARI with lower runtime on a two-component Gaussian mixture, plus a qualitative Old Faithful geyser illustration.

match_target.why: The Old Faithful result in Figure 1 is qualitative and the paper reports no numeric ARI or cluster label for it, so the cheapest quantitative central claim is GGDPC's n=500 ARI, which exercises the same density-gradient 1NN graph, center selection, and assignment pipeline under known mixture labels.

tolerance.why: Rule 3 applies: no standard deviation or confidence interval is printed for the target ARI, and ARI is a bounded score printed in [0,1] on an n=500 simulation, so the band is 0.02 absolute.

requirements.stmt: Compute the density estimate bp(Xi) and the gradient estimate bg(Xi)=∇bp(Xi) at every observation.
requirements.quote: Compute bp(Xi) and bg(Xi) for each observation Xi ∈Xn.

requirements.stmt: For every non-global-mode observation Xi, form the gradient-ascent update Xi+ηn bg(Xi), then choose the nearest observation Xj whose estimated density exceeds bp(Xi).
requirements.quote: Before searching for the 1NN of higher density, GGDPC takes a one-step gradient ascent from each observation and performs the 1NN uphill search around that update.

requirements.stmt: Impose the higher-density constraint relative to the original observation Xi, not the gradient-updated point.
requirements.quote: The gradient ascent update in (6) provides a stable search direction, while the density ordering remains anchored at the original observation.

requirements.stmt: Add a directed edge Xi to its gradient-guided 1NN uphill point and assign the uphill weight as the Euclidean distance between the point and Xi, with the global mode handled as the root with infinite/undefined outgoing weight.
requirements.quote: We also associate Xi with the weight bwn(Xi) defined in (7).

requirements.stmt: Select cluster centers by thresholding gradient-guided 1NN uphill distances; for the Figure 1 Old Faithful illustration use the sample mean plus three sample standard deviations as the threshold.
requirements.quote: The gray dashed line shows the distance threshold used in this illustration, equal to the sample mean uphill distance plus three sample standard deviations.

requirements.stmt: For the Table 1 simulation comparisons, select cluster centers as observations whose 1NN uphill distance exceeds the sample mean by at least four sample standard deviations.
requirements.quote: For DPC and GGDPC, we select observations whose 1NN uphill distances exceed the sample mean by at least four sample standard deviations as cluster centers.

requirements.stmt: Remove outgoing edges from selected centers and assign each remaining observation to the center reached by following its directed edges in the truncated graph.
requirements.quote: Each remaining observation is assigned to a cluster center by following its directed path in Gλ.

requirements.stmt: Produce the decision diagram with gradient-guided 1NN uphill distance on the horizontal axis and estimated density on the vertical axis, marking selected centers and the threshold line.
requirements.quote: the gradient-guided 1NN uphill distance plotted against estimated density.

requirements.stmt: Produce the density waterfall plot with GGDPC graph distance to the sample global mode on the horizontal axis and estimated density on the vertical axis.
requirements.cite: Section 7.2; Figure 1 caption, top right panel
requirements.quote: which displays estimated density against GGDPC graph distance to the sample global mode

requirements.stmt: Compute the GGDPC graph distance as the sum of Euclidean edge lengths along the unique directed path to the sample global-mode root.
requirements.quote: For any Xi̸ = X∗, let Xi ≡Xi1 →Xi2 →· · · →XiTi ≡X∗denote its unique directed path in G

requirements.stmt: Construct the GGDPC dendrogram by thresholding edge weights, taking connected components with edge directions ignored, so partitions refine as the threshold decreases.
requirements.quote: The second is a GGDPC dendrogram, obtained by thresholding gradient-guided 1NN uphill distances and following how graph components merge as the threshold increases.

requirements.stmt: Equivalently build a single-linkage dendrogram from the dissimilarity matrix with adjacent-pair distances ||Xi-Xj|| and a common d* larger than every edge weight for nonadjacent pairs.
requirements.quote: Applying single linkage clustering to D then yields the same hierarchy as thresholding the GGDPC graph directly.

requirements.stmt: For the Old Faithful illustration, use the 272 recorded eruptions, construct pairs of consecutive eruption durations (current and next), and apply GGDPC with Gaussian KDE.
requirements.quote: GGDPC applied to pairs of consecutive eruption durations in the Old Faithful data.

requirements.stmt: Do not use ground-truth labels to tune GGDPC on the Gaussian-mixture simulations.
requirements.quote: despite using no ground-truth information for parameter tuning.

data.name: Old Faithful Geyser data (Azzalini and Bowman, 1990)
data.how_to_get: Public Old Faithful eruption data with 272 eruptions; in R this is available as the base `faithful` dataset with columns `eruptions` and `waiting`. Use the `eruptions` sequence to form consecutive current-next eruption-duration pairs for Figure 1.

data.name: Two-component Gaussian-mixture simulation
data.how_to_get: Synthetic data from 0.5 N((0,0),0.09 I2)+0.5 N((1,0),0.09 I2); generate n=500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 8000 as in Table 1 and Figure 2.

data.name: GGDPC reference implementation
